subject.title: fix(codex): align watchdog defer guards and add wall-clock ceiling (#99272)

question: Should the Codex plugin own an independent absolute per-turn ceiling, and if so must that ceiling be derived from the effective run budget rather than fixed at 60 minutes?
rationale: The repository already has core and attempt-level timeout ownership, while this PR introduces a second absolute policy that can conflict with configured budgets; code inspection cannot determine the intended product boundary safely.

options.title: Derive from run budget
options.body: Keep a Codex-owned safety ceiling but calculate it from the effective attempt budget with focused shorter-, equal-, and longer-budget coverage.

options.title: Keep timeout in core
options.body: Drop the plugin-local wall-clock ceiling and let the existing core supervisor remain the sole absolute runtime owner.

options.title: Accept fixed 60 minutes
options.body: Land the independent constant as an intentional policy and document and prove its behavior against shorter and longer configured run budgets.

recommendation.title: Derive from run budget
recommendation.body: Keep a Codex-owned safety ceiling but calculate it from the effective attempt budget with focused shorter-, equal-, and longer-budget coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent integration history places this person closest to the Codex app-server and core timeout ownership boundary.
